item.text:
Continued the audit with a check of whether commit-index persistence covers commits that advance without a new append.

New low-severity observation, now reproduced:

- A live leader reached `commitIndex=12` while its commit-tracking store still returned `11` after ten applied commands. The same path also applies when a follower advances its commit index via a heartbeat with no new entries.
- Consequence: `RestoreCommittedLogs` may replay fewer recently committed commands than advertised, although the entries remain in the log and a live leader will re-establish the commit index. This appears conservative rather than a safety violation, so it is recorded separately from the two main findings.

Added test and evidence: `TestAuditCommitIndexPersistenceOnHeartbeatOnlyCommit` and `audit_results/finding4_commit_index_lag.txt`. I also added a passing control showing that a fresh-FSM restart with a snapshot plus 50 post-snapshot commits applies all 150 commands, confirming command replay itself works and isolating the main membership defect.

The report and reproduction script are updated:

- [report.md](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_16-03-24-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/report.md)
- [audit_restore_committed_config_test.go](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_16-03-24-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/audit_restore_committed_config_test.go)
- [reproduce_audit.sh](/home/nitro/Desktop/consensus-assurance/baseline/runs/2026-10-17_16-03-24-hashicorp_raft-baseline/work/reproduce_audit.sh)

The two main findings remain the committed-membership loss on restart and the `fsmMutateCh` startup deadlock. The remaining unverified edges are the `LogCache` optional-interface gap and commit-index behavior after snapshot installation.
